<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **4** package(s): `@objectstack/cli`, `@objectstack/core`, `@objectstack/spec`, `@objectstack/verify`, touching **4** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **3** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/cli/package.json`, `packages/cli/vitest.config.ts`, `packages/verify/package.json`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**1** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/permissions/capabilities.mdx`  _(via PLATFORM_CAPABILITY_TOKENS (symbol, a top-level const object))_

⛔ **1** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v16.mdx`  _(via PLATFORM_CAPABILITY_PROVIDERS (symbol, a top-level const object), PLATFORM_CAPABILITY_TOKENS (symbol, a top-level const object))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **3** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/cli/package.json`, `packages/cli/vitest.config.ts`, `packages/verify/package.json`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **2** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **69** of **252** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **183** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **183**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **124** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **192** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 9e6533bd484770298500ce4f03be2925d7986923` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `585611e57551fca67718e198e74bd12219b128a4` — the merge of head `6c2df3a10dfe608192c6ce673a460a74f7421aaa` into base `9e6533bd484770298500ce4f03be2925d7986923`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 585611e57551fca67718e198e74bd12219b128a4 && git checkout 585611e57551fca67718e198e74bd12219b128a4
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 9e6533bd484770298500ce4f03be2925d7986923 6c2df3a10dfe608192c6ce673a460a74f7421aaa && git checkout -B drift-repro 9e6533bd484770298500ce4f03be2925d7986923 && git merge --no-ff 6c2df3a10dfe608192c6ce673a460a74f7421aaa

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 9e6533bd484770298500ce4f03be2925d7986923
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 9e6533bd484770298500ce4f03be2925d7986923` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `6c2df3a10dfe608192c6ce673a460a74f7421aaa`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/kernel/platform-capabilities.ts, packages/spec/src/stack.zod.ts, skills/objectstack-platform/SKILL.md, skills/objectstack-project/references/platform-catalog.md + packages/core/src/capability-providers.ts, packages/spec/scripts/lib/platform-catalog.ts, packages/spec/scripts/platform-catalog.test.ts, scripts/check-skills-token-ratchet.mjs, packages/cli/package.json, packages/verify/package.json
Security-touching: yes

The `yes` is meant: the changed hunks (spec token comment, core row comment, both skills rows) teach which declaration exposes a caller-scoped record-read tool (`get_record_context`, `data:read`) to external MCP clients. No permission logic changes; the read stays bound to the caller in code outside this diff.

Inputs read: card #37189 body and its 8 comments (through 7166650889), the PR body, the 17-file net diff against `main`, and the check-runs on the head (no failure; every Test Core shard, every Lint and Type Check lane, Check Changeset, Spec property liveness and Governed Surface Queue Guard are `success`; the rest are `skipped` opt-in lanes). Nothing was built or run.

### ① Derived judgments

- **`requires` accept set widens by one token, `record-context`.** Right. It is appended to `PLATFORM_CAPABILITY_TOKENS`, the one list `defineStack` checks; kebab-case, as the file header requires. No alias is added, so `record_context` / `recordContext` stay unknown tokens.
- **`PLATFORM_CAPABILITY_PROVIDERS['record-context']` = `{ package: '@objectstack/service-record-context', edition: 'open' }`.** Right. Same shape as every open sibling (`push`, `mailbox`, `sms`); the package exists in the tree, is public (`publishConfig.access: public`) and exports `RecordContextServicePlugin`.
- **Not on `PLATFORM_ALWAYS_ON_CAPABILITIES`.** Right, and it is what the card's 「不按有情境包就自动挂」 asks for. The slate on the head is unchanged (11 tokens, none of them this one).
- **`CAPABILITY_PROVIDERS['record-context']` in `@objectstack/core`** (`pkg`, `export: 'RecordContextServicePlugin'`, identities `com.objectstack.service.record-context` and the class name). Right. The first identity is the plugin's real `name` in `packages/services/service-record-context/src/plugin.ts`; the package names agree between the spec row and the core row; no `configKey`, and the plugin's constructor takes no argument.
- **`@objectstack/cli` and `@objectstack/verify` gain a runtime dependency on the provider package.** Right, and required: `CapabilityEdition` defines `open` as "bundled as a dependency of `@objectstack/cli`", and `required-providers.ts` states every table package is a dependency of `@objectstack/verify`.
- **`aiContexts` `.describe()` text changes; the generated reference follows.** Right as a description-only change: no key, type or accept-set moves in `stack.zod.ts`.
- **Two published skill tables each gain the token.** Right: the `requires` table cell in `skills/objectstack-platform/SKILL.md` and the generated capability table in `platform-catalog.md` (`open`, `on requires`, derived from the spec rows above).
- **Hosted runtime.** The token is now accepted by the shared vocabulary but served only by the open readers. Right for this card: it rules the hosted kernel out of scope and names cloud#4978 as the carrier; the vocabulary header defines the list as the union of what the CLI and the cloud loader resolve.

### ② Semver level

`.changeset/37189-record-context-capability.md` is `minor` on `@objectstack/spec`, `@objectstack/core`, `@objectstack/cli` and `@objectstack/verify`. That matches what the diff publishes: an additive accept-set member and public-table row (spec), an additive provider row (core), and a new served capability with its dependency in both readers (cli, verify). Nothing is removed or narrowed, so nothing above minor is owed; `@objectstack/service-record-context` itself is unchanged and correctly not bumped. Check Changeset is `success` on the head.

Clause-②: `yes` on the PR body and on the changeset, and it is the right value: the diff widens an authorable accept set and two public tables. `Metadata-protocol: added` and `Skills-docs: follow-up #37177` appear in both places and agree.

### ③ Boundary flags

Dev flags (reports 7165118611 and 7166650889), each answered:

- **Dependencies, lockfile and the cli vitest alias outside the named surface.** Accepted: forced by the `open` edition's own definition and by the readers (see ①).
- **`serve.ts` not edited.** Correct against the tree: the resolver loop in `serve.ts` (step 5) reads `Serve.CAPABILITY_PROVIDERS[cap]`, a handle over the core table, skips on `providesCapability` over `plugins` and the resolver's own mounts, and constructs with no argument when `resolveCapabilityArgument` answers none. `constructServedProviders` in `@objectstack/verify` reads the same table by the same rule. The card's "readers in the same PR" is met by the shared table.
- **The `.describe()` line taken as the card's docs line.** Accepted with one correction: the report's "no hand-written docs page documents `get_record_context` today" is not accurate. `packages/services/service-record-context/README.md` is hand-written and still shows only the `plugins[]` mount, as does the plugin's docblock. Both are outside this diff and fenced for this card; see N2.
- **The verify `test-budget: 20` line now names nine boots, CI re-measure owed.** A test file, so the lane seat's remainder; Test Core is green on the head. The re-measure stays owed to the lane seat's ACCEPT.
- **Open question (the token forces three skills-side paths): answered** by the surface amendment 7165168860, and the route it names is in the tree: `lanes/skills.md` (the enumeration-row exception and its ceiling line) and the standing case in the header of `scripts/check-skills-token-ratchet.mjs`. `PLATFORM_CAPABILITY_TOKENS` is a symbol `check-skill-identifier-liveness` binds (Leg 2), so the SKILL.md row is squarely the case. The diff carries only enumeration rows: no teaching, example or eval.
- **Escalated to the maintainer's Tier H approval, one point.** The catalog ceiling (`HAND_WRITTEN_CEILING_TOKENS`, 1719 to 1726) is not a `CEILINGS` row of the skills ratchet; it lives in `platform-catalog.test.ts`, whose own header says a raise "cut[s] restated text first". The PR raises it with nothing cut, applying the standing enumeration-row case (ruling A on #32584, #32673 letter A) to this second ceiling by the seat's amendment. The reading is reasonable (same token, same kind of row, a published skill page, raised by exactly the row's 27 bytes), but it extends the ruling's words ("that file's row") to a ceiling they do not name. Approving this PR approves that reading.
- **Trailer and PR-body footer deviations.** Process only; no contract effect.

SQL push-down: the diff adds no query, no id materialisation and no in-app join. No finding.

`open_questions` in the final report: empty.

### ④ Design judgment

No must-fix, no should-fix.

**`packages/spec/src/kernel/platform-capabilities.ts`** — holds. The comment cites ADR-0160 D5; D5 places the service in `@objectstack/service-record-context` and says "a host without the service registers no `get_record_context` and nothing else changes", which the requested-only token preserves. The "requested, never always-on" rule is the card's, and the slate confirms it. Attempts to break it: (a) plugin order: the MCP plugin reads the `record-context` service in `start()`, after every `init()` has registered services, so resolver mount order cannot hide the tool; (b) double mount: a host instance matches by exact `name` or class name, in `plugins[]` and in the resolver's own mounts; (c) the token with MCP switched off: the service registers and no door reads it, nothing else changes; (d) near misses fall through to the unknown-token refusal because no alias exists.

**`packages/spec/src/stack.zod.ts`** — holds; one nit (N1). The added clause is true for the first consumer the card names (`os serve` and `bootStack` on a stack that declares the token).

**`skills/objectstack-platform/SKILL.md`** — holds against the spec it teaches. The cell reads "`@objectstack/service-` + the token", which yields `@objectstack/service-record-context`, the package in both tables. The token carries no `°`, correct for a token off the always-on slate. The card sets no eval prompt for this row; teaching and evals ride #37177.

**`skills/objectstack-project/references/platform-catalog.md`** — holds. The row is generated: `record-context` / `get_record_context over MCP` / `open` / `on requires`, each cell agreeing with `CAPABILITY_ROWS`, the provider row's edition and the slate.

Implementing files, against the contract:

- **`packages/core/src/capability-providers.ts`** — agrees sentence by sentence with the spec row and with the plugin (name, export, package). The comment's "without the token no tool and no service" is true of the resolver loop.
- **`packages/spec/scripts/lib/platform-catalog.ts`** — one `CAPABILITY_ROWS` line, 27 bytes of hand-written text; the catalog's exhaustiveness guard requires exactly one line per token.
- **`packages/spec/scripts/platform-catalog.test.ts`** — arithmetic holds: 6875 + 27 = 6902 bytes, ceil(6902 / 4) = 1726, pinned at the measurement. The authority for raising without a cut is the escalated point in ③.
- **`scripts/check-skills-token-ratchet.mjs`** — arithmetic holds against the blobs: the file is 24597 bytes on the merge base and 24614 on the head; less the 20-byte stamp, 24577 and 24594; ceil(24594 / 4) = 6149. The row adds 17 bytes, the 3 tokens of headroom are absorbed, the ceiling moves by 1 and no more, and nothing else in the file changed. Both rulings are cited in the comment and quoted in the PR body, as the standing case requires.
- **`packages/cli/package.json`, `packages/verify/package.json`** — one dependency line each, in sorted position; they make the `open` row's promise true.

Nits (no effect on correctness or the contract):

- N1 (nit) — `stack.zod.ts`: "which is served where `requires` includes `record-context`" can be read as the only condition. A host that mounts `RecordContextServicePlugin` in `plugins[]` serves the tool without the token, and the hosted runtime does not serve it yet (the changeset says so; the description does not). Not on a prose face, so left as an accepted deviation; #37177 can carry the fuller sentence.
- N2 (nit) — card item 5 is delivered only on the generated reference. The hand-written `packages/services/service-record-context/README.md` and the plugin docblock ("Composition is explicit: mount it in `plugins[]`") stay token-silent. Both are outside this diff and fenced by another open PR; the report names no carrier for them. Follow-up: add them to #37177.

## 维护者速读

- 改了什么：应用在配置里声明「记录情境」能力，开源运行时就自动挂上情境包服务，外部 AI 经 MCP 能读到单条记录的情境包；包括只发布编译产物的应用。不声明的部署完全不变。
- 为什么：记录范围 AI 问答专题的一步；此前只有宿主手写代码挂服务才有这个工具，纯元数据应用写了情境包也没人读。
- 风险：只影响声明了该能力的应用，最坏是该工具缺失；对外技能文件各补了一行能力名单（受管面），两处字数上限按实测增量各抬一点。
- 要你做什么：批准合并。契约复核 PASS 在评论 7166850191，Head-sha `6c2df3a10dfe608192c6ce673a460a74f7421aaa`。

席位意见：ACCEPT。行为、测试和产物启动都对得上卡；契约复核无必改项，两条小问题转后续卡。

## 席位核对

Head-sha: `6c2df3a10dfe608192c6ce673a460a74f7421aaa`
**ACCEPT** — L1, seat repo:objectstack#5

1. **Shape**: open draft against `main`; first line `Fixes #37189`, and merging delivers the whole card (acceptance 1–4 pinned below; item 5's docs line is the regenerated `aiContexts` reference, the rest rides #37177, see 5). No closing keyword binds another card. `l1-face` CLEAN, 13 items.
2. **Premise measured**: `os serve` and `bootStack` both read `CAPABILITY_PROVIDERS` (serve.ts imports the one table; `constructServedProviders` is the verify reader), so no reader edit is owed; the core row's first identity equals `RecordContextServicePlugin.name` (`com.objectstack.service.record-context`, read in the plugin source). Acceptance: token + pack → `tools/list` carries `get_record_context` and a call answers the pack; no-token control → no tool; host-mounted stand-in → no second mount (`harness.required-providers.test.ts`, three boots). Artifact boot (`os build` + `os serve` with no config) is the dev's container run in the PR body, with its no-token control. Ablation of the core row reds the token case only and the cli vocabulary pins; restored.
3. **Gates**: check-runs at `6c2df3a10d`: 64 success, 11 expected skip, 0 failed, 0 pending; Lint & Repo Gates and TypeScript Type Check `success`; mergeable clean. Changeset read sentence by sentence against the diff: true (minor on spec, core, cli, verify; near misses refused; host mount kept; hosted runtime not covered). Generated reference line matches the new `.describe()`.
4. **Accepted deviations**: (a) the verify file's `test-budget: 20` now covers nine boots and its CI re-measure is owed, as its own line says; (b) the catalog hand-written ceiling (1719 → 1726, +27 bytes) is raised under the enumeration-row case of ruling A on #32584 / #32673 letter A, which the contract record notes names the skills ratchet's `CEILINGS` rather than this test's ceiling — left to the maintainer's Tier H approval, not graded; (c) contract record nit N1 (the `aiContexts` description reads the token as the only serving condition).
5. **Out of scope and where it went**: `Skills-docs: follow-up #37177` is true (rows only here; teaching, examples, evals there). Contract nit N2 (the service package README and the plugin docblock still show only the `plugins[]` mount) and N1 go to #37177 through the area. Hosted kernel: objectstack-ai/cloud#4978.
6. **Landing terms**: Tier H (`skills/**`), whole PR. L2 at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`: PASS, comment 7166850191, same head, no must-fix, no should-fix; `Security-touching: yes` (it teaches which declaration exposes a caller-scoped read tool to MCP clients; no permission logic changes). Waits for the approver; the seat lands it after approval (ready, auto-merge, queue).
